property_summary: For any call to fallback with any sender and timestamp/block, the reference contract only accepts exactly 10 ether payments (call succeeds and updates pastBlockTime) whereas the mutant incorrectly accepts 9 ether, so the property is that calls with value == 10 ether succeed (and set pastBlockTime > previous) for all inputs while the mutant will behave differently for value == 10 ether (it will revert) or accept 9 ether — the fuzzer will find values distinguishing behavior.

For any caller and block timestamp, calling the fallback with exactly 10 ether always succeeds on the correct contract (updating pastBlockTime), whereas the mutant that requires 9 ether will cause a call with 10 ether to revert — so the rule: sending 10 ether to fallback must succeed (assert True), which the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any caller and block state, sending exactly 10 ether to C's fallback must succeed (not revert) and thus the call should return normally; the mutant that requires 9 ether will cause at least some such 10-ether calls to revert, breaking this rule.

For any caller and block timestamp/number, sending exactly 10 ether to C's payable fallback must succeed (not revert) and update pastBlockTime so that block.timestamp > previous pastBlockTime; the mutant that requires 9 ether will cause at least some 10-ether calls to revert, violating this rule.

For any caller and block state, sending exactly 10 ether to C's payable fallback must succeed (not revert); the mutant that changed the required amount to 9 ether will cause at least some such 10-ether calls to revert, violating this rule.

For any call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether, the reference contract C only updates pastBlockTime when the block timestamp strictly increases (i.e., after the call pastBlockTime > previous pastBlockTime), while the mutant may update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, breaking this monotonicity property for some inputs.

After any successful fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether, the reference contract ensures pastBlockTime strictly increases relative to its prior value when block.timestamp increases; the mutant can set pastBlockTime regardless of timestamp ordering, breaking the monotonicity relation for some inputs.

For any fallback call sending exactly 10 ether, the reference contract only allows pastBlockTime to increase when block.timestamp is strictly greater than its previous value; the mutant can update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp does not advance, violating monotonicity when calls occur at the same timestamp.

For any call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether, the reference contract never updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is less than or equal to its previous stored value (i.e., pastBlockTime only advances when block.timestamp strictly increases); the mutant removes that timestamp check and can update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp hasn't advanced, violating this monotonicity rule for some inputs.

For any caller and timestamp, if fallback is called with exactly 10 ether while block.timestamp has not advanced since the last successful update, the correct contract refuses to update pastBlockTime (it preserves monotonicity), whereas the mutant can update pastBlockTime even when timestamp did not advance, so there exist inputs (two calls at same timestamp) that make their stored pastBlockTime differ.

For any caller and any block.timestamp such that the fallback call succeeds, the contract's pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the timestamp at which the call executed (reference sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1), whereas the mutant that sets pastBlockTime = block.timestamp can make pastBlockTime equal to the call timestamp; the test fuzzes caller and timestamp and detects when pastBlockTime == block.timestamp (buggy) which never happens in the reference.

For every call to fallback sending exactly 10 ether and with block.timestamp strictly greater than the stored pastBlockTime, the reference contract only empties its balance when block.number % 15 == 0, so address(c).balance == 0 iff block.number % 15 == 0; the mutant inverts the condition and will make address(c).balance == 0 for block.number % 15 != 0, violating this rule for some block numbers.

For every call to fallback that sends exactly 10 ether and occurs at a strictly later timestamp, when block.number % 15 == 0 the reference contract forwards its entire balance to the caller (leaving address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant only sends 1 ether so address(c).balance may remain > 0 for some inputs.

For any caller and timestamp where the fallback call is admissible (sends exactly 10 ether and occurs after the stored pastBlockTime), whenever the block number is a multiple of 15 the reference contract will forward its entire balance away (leaving address(c).balance == 0), whereas the mutant that transfers only 1 ether can leave a nonzero contract balance; the test asserts address(c).balance == 0 after such a call — this holds for the reference for all inputs but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

Whenever a valid fallback call (msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) is made at a block where block.number % 15 == 0, the reference contract forwards its entire balance so address(c).balance == 0 after the call; the mutant that transfers only 1 ether can leave a nonzero contract balance and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For every admissible call to fallback (msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) made at any block, if the contract's balance before the call is exactly 10 ether then the reference forwards the entire contract balance to caller when block.number % 15 == 0 (leaving address(c).balance == 0) while the mutant that transfers only 1 ether can leave a nonzero balance; thus: whenever pre-call balance == 10 ether and call is valid at block%15==0, address(c).balance == 0 after the call (reference always satisfies, mutant broken for some fuzzed inputs).

For any admissible fallback call (msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) made when block.number % 15 == 0 and the contract has a pre-call balance strictly greater than 1 ether, the reference forwards the entire contract balance to the caller (leaving address(c).balance == 0) while the mutant that only transfers 1 ether can leave a nonzero contract balance.

After any successful fallback call sending exactly 10 ether and with block.timestamp > prior pastBlockTime, the reference sets pastBlockTime == block.timestamp + 1, whereas the mutant sometimes sets it to block.timestamp + 2 (so the getter pastBlockTime differs).

After a successful fallback call that transfers exactly 10 ether and where block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the contract's pastBlockTime is updated to a strictly greater value (pastBlockTime == old timestamp + 1); the mutant that omits the assignment leaves pastBlockTime unchanged and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any block where block.timestamp > pastBlockTime and caller sends exactly 10 ether, the reference contract always updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 after a successful fallback call, but the mutant can fail to update pastBlockTime when the conditional transfer occurs (i.e., when block.number % 15 == 0 and the transfer reverts), so there exists inputs (a caller whose receive reverts and a block.number divisible by 15) where the mutant leaves pastBlockTime unchanged while the reference updates it.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether at a time when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference contract always updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 after the fallback call completes; the mutant can fail to update pastBlockTime when an external transfer to the caller reverts (e.g., when block.number % 15 == 0 and the recipient's fallback reverts).

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, contract C always updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp + 1 after the fallback call completes; the mutant can fail to update pastBlockTime when the conditional transfer attempts to send to a callee whose fallback reverts (i.e., when block.number % 15 == 0 and the recipient reverts).

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the correct contract always updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 after the fallback call completes; the mutant can fail to update pastBlockTime when the contract attempts the conditional transfer and that external transfer fails (e.g. recipient reverts) before the assignment, so pastBlockTime remains unchanged.

For any caller sending exactly 10 ether when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the reference C always updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp+1 after fallback returns; the mutant can fail to update pastBlockTime when the contract's conditional transfer to the caller reverts (e.g., when block.number % 15 == 0 and the recipient reverts), leaving pastBlockTime unchanged.
